titleEn: From Demo to Deal: FIRA USA Connects Pacific Northwest Growers With Ag Robotics and Tech
titleZh: FIRA USA 2026：农业机器人从演示走向实际交易，连接太平洋西北种植者
summaryZh: FIRA USA 2026在华盛顿州雅基马闭幕，吸引20国2500余名参与者，其中600多名种植者。活动通过现场机器人演示和农场考察，将农业自动化技术直接对接太平洋西北地区高价值特色作物种植者，聚焦劳动力短缺下的喷洒、灌溉和采收自动化需求。文章介绍了巡回办展模式、区域产业生态构建及2027年移师佛罗里达的计划，对理解农业机器人商业化落地路径具有参考价值。
featuredReason: 虽然文章聚焦种植业机器人，但其“巡回办展、深入产区、对接真实需求”的模式对智慧畜牧行业推广物联网、AI和自动化技术具有直接借鉴意义，且文中关于劳动力短缺驱动自动化、ROI验证和区域生态构建的讨论同样适用于养殖业。
contentFull:
By GOFAR 

 

 Share

 

 

 

 

 

 FIRA USA 2026 closed its Pacific Northwest edition after three days that put agricultural robotics and AgTech in front of the growers who need them. From Oct. 20 to 22, more than 2,500 participants from 20 countries, including over 600 growers, attended live robot demonstrations, and tours of local farms and test plots. After California (2022-2025) and Washington (2026), FIRA USA will continue its journey in 2027.

 FIRA USA 2026 once again proved its value as a working platform where agricultural innovation meets the growers who carry it to the fields; by moving to a new region each year, GOFAR turns every edition into a starting point for lasting collaboration among farmers, technology providers, and investors, well beyond the three days. The result: growers arrived with concrete equipment plans, turning three days of demonstrations into real adoption decisions in the field.

 FIRA goes where innovation is needed in fields

 “We don’t believe innovation should wait for farmers to come to it. We believe innovation must go where it is needed,” said Aymeric Barthes, President, GOFAR.

 FIRA became a traveling event so innovation goes where it is needed: after four years in California, the 2026 U.S. edition took place in Yakima (WA), bringing robots to PNW growers.

 In every region, GOFAR studies local challenges, identifies useful technologies, and connects farmers, technology providers, and investors, active today on three continents. FIRA is also built for CEOs and product teams: a place to meet their peers, exchange on real-world challenges, and refine their products so they fit what the market expects, in the field, at scale, and at the right price.

 The 2026 edition confirmed the traveling event model as the right regional response to modern farming’s diverse realities.

 Why the PNW region mattered

 PNW is one of the U.S.’s most diverse and high-value specialty crop hubs—orchards, hops, vineyards, potatoes, onions, berries—facing acute labor shortages and looking for solutions that fit their scale.

 The turnout confirmed it: more than 2,500 participants, including over 600 growers, innovators from 20 countries (nearly 70% AgTech, equipment and robotics). Over half the farms exceed 1,000 acres (nearly 10% over 15,000); more than one-third of growers present are already investing in robotics, and over 80% see an urgent need for automation in spraying, irrigation and harvesting.

 “Yakima is not just a venue, it is a perfect testing ground: large-scale commercial farms, high-value crops, and the right conditions to run meaningful demonstrations of ROI and scalability,” said Maialen Cazenave, Co-Director, GOFAR – FIRA USA.

 The Pacific Northwest AgTech ecosystem now joins the broader GOFAR network, further reinforcing GOFAR’s position as the world’s largest agricultural robotics community.

 “I want to thank GOFAR for bringing FIRA USA to the Yakima Valley. This event has ignited the long lasting development of the ag-tech industry in our region and beyond,” highlighted Jonathan Smith, Executive Director of Yakima County Development Association.

 FIRA USA 2026 was co-organized by GOFAR, Yakima County Government, the Yakima County Development Association, with support from the Washington Tree Fruit Research Commission and the WSU College of Agricultural, Human, and Natural Resource Sciences.

 What’s next

 FIRA USA moves to Florida in 2027, in partnership with the University of Florida and hosted at the UF/IFAS Institute for Agricultural Innovation. A dedicated press release with details on the Florida edition, including dates, programming, and participation opportunities, will follow. GOFAR is active on three continents and in discussions to expand to five, building regional ecosystems that stay active well after each event moves on.

translationZh:
FIRA USA 2026在为期三天后闭幕了其太平洋西北地区站活动，这三天将农业机器人和农业科技直接呈现在需要它们的种植者面前。从10月20日至22日，来自20个国家的2500多名参与者，其中包括600多名种植者，参加了现场机器人演示以及当地农场和试验田的考察。继加利福尼亚（2022-2025年）和华盛顿（2026年）之后，FIRA USA将在2027年继续其旅程。

FIRA USA 2026再次证明了其作为工作平台的价值——农业创新在这里与将其带到田间的种植者相遇；通过每年迁移到新地区，GOFAR将每一届活动都变成农民、技术提供商和投资者之间持久合作的起点，远远超出这三天。结果是：种植者带着具体的设备计划而来，将三天的演示转化为田间真正的采用决策。

**FIRA去往田间需要创新的地方**

GOFAR总裁Aymeric Barthes表示：“我们不相信创新应该等待农民来找它。我们相信创新必须去往需要它的地方。”

FIRA成为巡回活动，是为了让创新去往需要它的地方：在加利福尼亚四年之后，2026年美国站活动在雅基马（华盛顿州）举办，将机器人带给了太平洋西北地区的种植者。

2026年届活动确认了巡回活动模式是应对现代农业多样化现实的正确区域响应。

**为什么太平洋西北地区重要**

太平洋西北地区是美国最多样化、最具高价值的特色作物中心之一——果园、啤酒花、葡萄园、马铃薯、洋葱、浆果——面临严重的劳动力短缺，并正在寻找适合其规模的解决方案。

参与人数证实了这一点：2500多名参与者，包括600多名种植者，来自20个国家的创新者（近70%为农业科技、设备和机器人领域）。超过一半的农场面积超过1000英亩（近10%超过15000英亩）；超过三分之一的到场种植者已在投资机器人技术，超过80%认为喷洒、灌溉和采收的自动化存在迫切需求。

GOFAR – FIRA USA联合总监Maialen Cazenave表示：“雅基马不仅仅是一个场地，它是一个完美的试验场：大规模商业农场、高价值作物，以及开展有意义的ROI和可扩展性演示的合适条件。”

太平洋西北地区农业科技生态系统现已加入更广泛的GOFAR网络，进一步巩固了GOFAR作为全球最大农业机器人社区的地位。

雅基马县发展协会执行董事Jonathan Smith强调：“我要感谢GOFAR将FIRA USA带到雅基马谷。这项活动点燃了我们地区及其他地区农业科技产业的长期发展。”

FIRA USA 2026由GOFAR、雅基马县政府、雅基马县发展协会共同组织，并得到华盛顿树木果研究委员会和WSU农业、人类与自然资源科学学院的支持。

**下一步**

FIRA USA将于2027年移至佛罗里达州，与佛罗里达大学合作，在UF/IFAS农业创新研究所举办。关于佛罗里达站活动的详细信息，包括日期、议程和参与机会，将随后发布专门新闻稿。GOFAR活跃于三大洲，并正在讨论扩展到五大洲，构建在每个活动移师后仍长期活跃的区域生态系统。
